text: You arrive on time for your doctor's appointment, feeling punctual. You expect to be seen quickly, right on schedule.
But after checking in, you sit in the waiting room. Minutes tick by. Other patients come and go, yet your turn is delayed.
You wonder: are they always this slow? Are they overbooked, cramming too many people in? It feels inefficient and frustrating.
The hidden system: a doctor never knows exactly how long each patient will take. Some are quick; others reveal complex issues.
To ensure every patient gets full, unhurried attention, the schedule builds in a crucial buffer. Your waiting time is that essential safety margin.
So next time you're waiting, you're not just stuck. You're part of an invisible system ensuring quality care for every patient, including you.
